annotations.title: Find pages that earn no clicks

description: Pages Google shows and nobody clicks: impressions above a floor with zero (or near-zero) clicks, split by CAUSE, because each cause needs a different fix. `branded`: at least half the page's named-query impressions are searches for the brand itself (its name, aliases or domain), so it is a secondary listing under a brand search; another page, named in `clickGoesTo` and usually the home page, takes that click, and no title work helps. `snippet`: position 10 or better on non-brand searches and still not clicked, so the title/meta description is losing the click, the cheapest fix. `page-two`: position above 10 and up to 15, where few searchers look, so a title change moves little until the page reaches page one. `ranking`: position beyond 15, too far down to be clicked; needs authority or a rewrite. Each row also carries `brandedPct`, `namedImpressions` (Google withholds rare queries, so this can be below `impressions`) and its top queries. Sorted by wasted impressions. This finds the single most common expensive miss in a content library: the page that earns the most impressions on the whole site and converts none of them. Requires a paid plan (Starter+).

domain.description: Bare domain, e.g. 'example.com'. Provide this OR siteUrl.

maxClicks.description: Treat a page as zero-click at or below this many clicks. Default 0.

minImpressions.description: Impression floor for a page to count. Default 25.

name: gsc_zero_click_pages
